facets.label: Mark Type
facets.description: the structural anatomy of the logo. wordmark = the full brand name set in distinctive type IS the logo; lettermark-monogram = initials or a single stylized letter only; pictorial-mark = a literal, recognizable image of a real-world thing; abstract-mark = a non-representational geometric symbol; mascot = an illustrated character with personality; emblem-badge = the name locked INSIDE a containing shape and inseparable from it (badges, seals, crest-style labels); combination-mark = symbol + wordmark paired side by side or stacked, where each could stand alone. If the image shows a whole identity system, classify the primary mark.

facets.label: Presentation Format
facets.description: what the image actually shows. isolated-mark = one logo on a plain background; lockup-variations = multiple arrangements/color-ways/responsive sizes of the same mark; in-context-mockup = logo applied to signage, packaging, merch, or screens; brand-sheet = a portfolio grid of marks or a full identity board with type/color specimens; construction-grid = the mark shown with its geometric scaffolding or proportion circles; process-sketches = pencil roughs or exploration pages.

facets.label: Aesthetic Archetype
facets.description: the dominant stylistic school. minimalist-modern = reduced, clean, contemporary-startup polish; geometric-modernist = strict circles/grids, Swiss-Bauhaus lineage (mid-century corporate modernism); corporate-classic = safe, conservative, blue-chip; luxury-elegant = hairline serifs, wide-tracked caps, refined monograms; playful-cartoon = bouncy, rounded, bright, cute; vintage-retro = deliberate era nostalgia of any decade (50s diner, 70s groovy, 80s chrome, Y2K); hand-crafted-artisanal = hand-drawn warmth, craft badges, imperfect strokes; tech-futuristic = sharp cuts, circuit/node motifs, sci-fi gradients; brutalist-experimental = raw, wonky, anti-polish, oversized or deliberately crude type. If both minimalist-modern and geometric-modernist fit, prefer geometric-modernist when the mark is built from visible strict geometry.

facets.label: Construction Techniques
facets.description: formal devices used to build the mark. Tag all that clearly apply; a plain flat mark may get none. negative-space = the empty space forms a hidden second image — only tag this if you can explicitly name what the hidden image depicts; monoline-linework = uniform single stroke weight throughout; letter-fusion = letters merged or sharing strokes into one glyph; overlap-transparency = layered semi-transparent shapes creating new colors where they intersect; gradient-blend = smooth color transitions, incl. aura/blur/thermal-style gradients; 3d-dimensional = extrusion, perspective, isometric or rendered depth; pixel-bitmap = visible square pixels; hand-drawn-brush = organic imperfect strokes or lettering; texture-grain = grain, distress, print noise, rubber-stamp texture; continuous-line = the whole figure traced by one unbroken line.

facets.label: Typography
facets.description: typeface classes present in any lettering; skip entirely if the mark contains no letters. serif includes high-contrast hairline styles typical of fashion and luxury; script = handwriting, calligraphy, signature styles; blackletter = gothic/fraktur forms; display-decorative = novelty headline faces fitting no classic class; monospace = fixed-width, code/terminal feel; rounded-friendly = sans with visibly rounded terminals; wonky-warped = deliberately misaligned, melted, stretched, or naive letterforms.

facets.label: Color Strategy
facets.description: how color is used in the mark itself, not the background or mockup scene. monochrome = black/white/one neutral; single-color = one brand hue; duotone = exactly two flat hues; multicolor = three or more flat hues; gradient = the mark is dominated by smooth color transitions; metallic = gold/silver/chrome/foil finishes.

facets.label: Dominant Shape
facets.description: the overall silhouette or container geometry. circular = roundels, rings, circle-bounded marks; shield-crest = heraldic shields, badges, wax seals; organic-fluid = blobs, waves, botanical curves; linear-horizontal = wide wordmark-driven silhouettes with no strong geometric container; asymmetric-freeform = dynamic compositions with no dominant geometry. For combination marks, judge the symbol rather than the full lockup.

facets.label: Figurative Motif
facets.description: what the mark literally depicts, if anything; leave untagged for purely abstract or type-only marks. celestial = sun, moon, stars, planets, orbits; crown-heraldry = crowns, laurels, ribbons, and other heraldic devices; everyday-object = tools, books, keys, hearts, and other man-made items; landscape-nature = mountains, waves-as-scenery, trees, fire.

facets.label: Industry Vibe
facets.description: the sector the brand appears to belong to, inferred from the name and styling. Tag only when reasonably confident; skip for ambiguous or concept work.

context: This gallery is a logo and brand-mark inspiration stash. Images include isolated marks, lockup variations, full brand-identity sheets, and logos applied to mockups, collected from portfolios and inspiration sites. Tag the primary mark in the image. All styles and industries are fair game — we're interested in the craft of the mark itself: its anatomy, construction, and styling.
